quote: Theorem 1. Let T ⇝ GMOTL − G (δ, ρ1 , ω ) and Y ⇝ GMOTL − G (δ, ρ2 , ω ). If ρ1 < ρ2 , then T ≤lr Y. As a consequence, it follows that (T ≤hr Y, T ≤rhr Y, T ≤st Y ).
family: GMOTL−G(δ, ρ, ω) family, pdf f GMOTLG (t; δ, ρ, ω ) = 2ρδ δωg(t) Ḡ (t)(1 − Ḡ (t)2 )ω−1 [1 − (1 − Ḡ (t)2 )ω ]δ−1 / [1 − ρ̄ (1 − (1 − Ḡ (t)2 )ω )]δ+1, Eq. (5); baseline G arbitrary
compared: Marshall-Olkin tilt parameter ρ1 vs ρ2; δ, ω and baseline G common

hypotheses.text: Let T ⇝ GMOTL − G (δ, ρ1 , ω ) and Y ⇝ GMOTL − G (δ, ρ2 , ω )
hypotheses.formal: T ~ GMOTL-G(δ, ρ1, ω), Y ~ GMOTL-G(δ, ρ2, ω)

hypotheses.text: T is said to be smaller than Y in the likelihood ratio order (denoted by T ≤lr Y) if the ratio f (t)/g(t) is decreasing in t, for all t ≥ 0

conclusion.direction: T <=lr Y; as a consequence T <=hr Y, T <=rhr Y, T <=st Y

quantifiers: δ, ρ1, ρ2, ω > 0; all t > 0
ambiguity: None material; the printed derivative of f/g contains factor (ρ1 − ρ2), consistent with ρ1 < ρ2 giving a decreasing ratio. Note ρ̄ = 1 − ρ is used; ρ can exceed 1 per the Marshall-Olkin construction mentioned earlier (ρ > 1 allowed there), so ρ̄ may be negative.
